public_rationale: ServiceNow completed its acquisition of Moveworks on December 15, 2025. Moveworks was an AI-focused software company with a previously announced multibillion-dollar private valuation. This contradicts the categorical statement that AI-company exits are impossible. It does not establish that every AI company can exit, that Moveworks was profitable, or that investors in the largest model developers will recover their valuations.
limitations: The verdict applies to the broad categorical wording, not a narrower claim about particular model developers.
The linked essay itself recognizes acquisition exceptions.
A completed exit does not prove sustainable economics or satisfactory returns for every investor.
If unsustainable is intended to define a narrower company class, that class needs an objective definition before the causal claim can be resolved.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI companies' inflated valuations and unsustainable businesses make exits or IPOs impossible.

statement.excerpt: AI companies' ridiculous valuations and unsustainable businesses make exits or IPOs impossible

our_interpretation: Read the statement as a categorical claim that AI-focused software companies cannot achieve genuine acquisition exits or IPOs because of their valuations and business economics.
Following the linked essay, exclude talent-hiring and licensing arrangements that do not acquire the company.
Do not restrict AI companies to the few largest model developers; that restriction is absent from the quoted statement.
No minimum investor return or requirement to exceed a previous valuation is stated.
The decisive test is completion of an exit transaction. No numerical valuation or accounting result is being graded; financial figures are contextual.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes that the described valuation and business constraints prevent genuine acquisition exits and IPOs across the claimed company class. Mere absence of transactions is insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A qualifying AI-focused software company completes a genuine acquisition exit or IPO despite the categorical assertion that such exits are impossible.

evidence.explanation: The announcement confirms a completed acquisition and describes Moveworks' AI assistant, enterprise search, and reasoning technology. It is a genuine company exit, contradicting the categorical claim that AI-company exits are impossible.

Moveworks had a multibillion-dollar private valuation, making it relevant to the valuation concern. This does not itself establish that the valuation was inflated, the business unsustainable, or every investor's exit profitable.
